items.q: A bar graph shows lunches sold: Monday 12, Tuesday 20, Wednesday 16. How many more lunches were sold on Tuesday than on Monday?
misconceptions: added the two bars instead of comparing them
compared Tuesday with Wednesday instead
correct
read Monday's bar again instead of the difference
items.why: How many more means compare: 20 - 12 = 8 more lunches on Tuesday.

items.q: On a picture graph, each picture stands for 2 books. One row shows 5 pictures. How many books is that?
misconceptions: counted the pictures and forgot each one stands for 2
added the scale to the count instead of multiplying
correct
multiplied 5 by itself instead of by the scale
items.why: The scale is the key: each picture is worth 2 books, so 5 pictures are 5 x 2 = 10 books.

items.q: Four ribbons measure 1/2, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/4 of a yard. Laid end to end, how long are they together?
misconceptions: kept only the two halves and dropped the quarters
rounded every piece up to a whole yard
added the tops and the bottoms, the old Jumble trick
correct
items.why: Add the like pieces: 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 yard, and 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2 yard. Together that is 1 1/2 yards.

items.q: A class wants to chart everyone's favorite fruit. Which question gives the best answers to chart?
choices: Why is fruit good for you?
What did you eat on your last birthday?
What is your favorite fruit: apple, banana, grape or pear?
misconceptions: its answers are reasons, not choices a chart can count
one day's eating is not a favorite, and every answer would differ
that is a yes or no fact, not a favorite to tally
correct
items.why: A good survey question offers a handful of clear choices that answers can be tallied and charted: apple, banana, grape or pear.

items.q: Five pencils measure 6, 7, 6, 8 and 6 inches. On a line plot of these lengths, how many marks stand over the 6?
misconceptions: counted every pencil, not just the ones over the 6
counted the other lengths instead
correct
read the length itself as the count
items.why: Count the pencils that measure 6 inches: the first, the third and the fifth. That is 3 marks over the 6.

items.q: A class wants to know how students get to school. Which is a good survey question?
choices: How do you get to school: walk, bus, car or bike?
misconceptions: it asks why about a bus, not how anyone travels
correct
everyone shares one answer, so there is nothing to compare
it asks about liking, not about getting to school
items.why: The question must match the job and offer choices to tally: walk, bus, car or bike.

items.q: A spinner has 6 equal parts and only 1 part is red. Landing on red is...
misconceptions: certain would mean every part is red
red can land, so it is not impossible
an even chance would need half the parts to be red
correct
items.why: Only 1 of the 6 equal parts is red, so red can happen but probably will not: that is unlikely.

items.q: Every face of a cube is painted blue. Rolling a blue face is...
misconceptions: likely still leaves room for another result, and there is none
correct
blue is the only face there is
blue is the only face there is, so it must land
items.why: Every face is blue, so blue is the only result there can be: that is certain.

items.q: A bag holds 4 red counters and 4 blue counters. Picking a red counter is...
misconceptions: half the counters are blue, so red is not certain
half the counters are red, so red is not unlikely
correct
there are red counters in the bag, so red can be picked
items.why: The bag is split in half: 4 red out of 8 counters. Half and half is an even chance.

items.q: How many meters are in 3 kilometers 400 meters?
misconceptions: shrunk the 400 meters to 40 on the way
put a zero where the 400's own place belongs
correct
added a zero to the whole measure
items.why: 3 kilometers is 3 x 1,000 = 3,000 meters, and 3,000 + 400 = 3,400 meters.

items.q: A rope 3 meters long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
misconceptions: glued the two numbers together instead of sharing the rope
kept the whole rope for one piece
shared 1 meter instead of the whole 3 meters
correct
items.why: Share 3 meters into 4 equal pieces: each is 3/4 of a meter, and 3/4 of 100 centimeters is 75 centimeters.

items.q: The Vault tour starts at 10:40 and lasts 35 minutes. When does it end?
misconceptions: added the minutes but never traded 60 for an hour
stopped 10 minutes early
correct
added only 15 of the 35 minutes
items.why: Hop the line: 10:40 plus 20 minutes reaches 11:00, and 15 minutes more lands on 11:15.
